questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman has had 8 months of worsening shortness of breath on exertion. Last week she fainted while climbing stairs. Her mother died at age 40 of high blood pressure in the lungs. The pulmonic component of S2 is loud, and there is a left parasternal heave. Echocardiography shows right ventricular hypertrophy, a high estimated pulmonary artery pressure, a normal left ventricle and no shunt. Pulmonary function tests and a ventilation-perfusion scan are normal. Genetic testing finds a heterozygous loss-of-function mutation in BMPR2. How does this mutation most likely cause her disease?
choices: Constant activation of endothelin receptors on arterial smooth muscle
Defective fibrillin that weakens the media of the pulmonary arteries
Loss of a signal that normally restrains vascular cell growth
Gain of function of a tyrosine kinase in endothelial cells
Abnormal type III collagen that makes arterial walls fragile
questions.explanation: **BMPR2** is a receptor of the **TGF-β family** whose signaling normally holds back the growth of pulmonary arterial smooth muscle and endothelium. **Loss of function** removes this brake, so the arteries develop **medial hypertrophy**, intimal fibrosis and **plexiform lesions**, which raise pulmonary vascular resistance. Endothelin is overproduced in pulmonary arterial hypertension and is a drug target, but the mutation does not act by switching on endothelin receptors.
questions.explanation_pt: O **BMPR2** é um receptor da **família do TGF-β** cuja sinalização normalmente freia o crescimento do músculo liso e do endotélio das artérias pulmonares. A **perda de função** remove esse freio, e as artérias desenvolvem **hipertrofia da média**, fibrose da íntima e **lesões plexiformes**, que aumentam a resistência vascular pulmonar. A endotelina é produzida em excesso na hipertensão arterial pulmonar e é alvo de fármacos, mas a mutação não age ativando os receptores de endotelina.

questions.stem: A 71-year-old woman with long-standing hypertension and obesity has 1 year of shortness of breath on exertion, shortness of breath when lying flat, and ankle swelling. Echocardiography shows a left ventricular ejection fraction of 62%, thick left ventricular walls, an enlarged left atrium and no shunt. Right heart catheterization shows right atrial pressure 14 mm Hg (normal 2-6), mean pulmonary artery pressure 36 mm Hg (normal about 15), and pulmonary capillary wedge pressure 24 mm Hg (normal 6-12). What is the most likely mechanism of her pulmonary hypertension?
choices: High left atrial pressure transmitted back into the lungs
Overgrowth of the arterial wall from a BMPR2 mutation
Arteriolar constriction in response to low alveolar oxygen
Organized blood clots blocking the pulmonary arteries
Extra pulmonary blood flow from a left-to-right shunt
questions.explanation: A **high wedge pressure** means the left atrial pressure is high, so the pulmonary hypertension starts **after the capillaries**. A stiff, thick left ventricle (heart failure with preserved ejection fraction) raises left atrial pressure, which passes back into the pulmonary veins and arteries; **left-heart disease is the most common cause** of pulmonary hypertension. BMPR2 disease, hypoxic vasoconstriction and chronic clots all raise pulmonary artery pressure **with a normal wedge pressure**, so they do not fit these numbers.
questions.explanation_pt: Uma **pressão de oclusão (encunhamento) alta** indica pressão alta no átrio esquerdo, então a hipertensão pulmonar começa **depois dos capilares**. Um ventrículo esquerdo espesso e rígido (insuficiência cardíaca com fração de ejeção preservada) eleva a pressão no átrio esquerdo, que é transmitida às veias e artérias pulmonares; a **doença do coração esquerdo é a causa mais comum** de hipertensão pulmonar. A doença por BMPR2, a vasoconstrição hipóxica e os coágulos crônicos elevam a pressão da artéria pulmonar **com pressão de oclusão normal**, então não explicam esses valores.

questions.stem: A 64-year-old man with pancreatic cancer suddenly collapses at home. Blood pressure is 78/50 mm Hg, pulse is 128/min, and oxygen saturation is 84% on room air. His neck veins are distended, and his lungs are clear. A bedside echocardiogram shows a very large right ventricle. The interventricular septum is flat and bulges toward the left ventricle, and the left ventricle is small and contracts strongly. There is no pericardial fluid. Which mechanism best explains his low blood pressure?
choices: Loss of left ventricular contraction from a blocked coronary artery
Fluid in the pericardial sac that limits filling of both ventricles
Widespread dilation of arterioles that lowers systemic resistance
Loss of circulating volume that lowers venous return to the heart
Right ventricular overload that underfills the left ventricle
questions.explanation: Cancer is a hypercoagulable state, and this picture fits a **massive pulmonary embolism**. The sudden rise in pulmonary resistance makes the thin right ventricle **dilate and fail**; the septum is pushed into the left ventricle, and little blood crosses the lungs, so **left ventricular filling and cardiac output fall**. Cardiac tamponade also causes hypotension with distended neck veins, but the echo shows no pericardial fluid and a small, strongly contracting left ventricle with a huge right ventricle.
questions.explanation_pt: O câncer é um estado de hipercoagulabilidade, e o quadro é de **embolia pulmonar maciça**. O aumento súbito da resistência pulmonar faz o ventrículo direito, de parede fina, **dilatar e entrar em falência**; o septo é empurrado para o ventrículo esquerdo, e pouco sangue atravessa os pulmões, então o **enchimento do ventrículo esquerdo e o débito cardíaco caem**. O tamponamento cardíaco também causa hipotensão com estase jugular, mas o ecocardiograma não mostra derrame pericárdico e mostra ventrículo esquerdo pequeno e hipercontrátil com ventrículo direito muito dilatado.

questions.stem: A 54-year-old man takes high-dose methadone for opioid use disorder. His wife says he often stops breathing during sleep, but he does not snore. His BMI is 23 kg/m², and his neck and throat look normal. Overnight polysomnography shows many 20-second pauses in nasal airflow. During each pause, the chest and abdominal belts show no movement at all, and oxygen saturation falls to 84%. Which mechanism best explains these pauses?
choices: Collapse of the pharyngeal airway when muscle tone falls
Blunted CO2 response of the medullary respiratory centers
Weakness of the diaphragm from injury to the phrenic nerves
Narrowing of small airways from histamine released by mast cells
Stiff lungs that need more work to inflate during sleep
questions.explanation: Pauses in airflow with **no chest or abdominal movement** mean there is **no respiratory effort**: this is **central sleep apnea**. Opioids act on **mu receptors in the brainstem** and blunt the response of the respiratory centers to **carbon dioxide**, so the drive to breathe disappears during sleep. In obstructive sleep apnea the pharynx collapses, but the chest and abdomen keep moving against the closed airway, and the patient usually snores and is often obese.
questions.explanation_pt: Pausas no fluxo de ar **sem movimento torácico ou abdominal** indicam **ausência de esforço respiratório**: trata-se de **apneia central do sono**. Os opioides agem nos **receptores mu do tronco encefálico** e reduzem a resposta dos centros respiratórios ao **dióxido de carbono**, então o estímulo para respirar desaparece durante o sono. Na apneia obstrutiva do sono, a faringe colapsa, mas o tórax e o abdome continuam se movendo contra a via aérea fechada, e o paciente costuma roncar e muitas vezes é obeso.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old man had an esophagectomy for esophageal cancer 4 days ago. He started eating again yesterday. Since then, a large volume of milky white, odorless fluid has drained from his right chest tube. He has no fever. Pleural fluid analysis shows triglycerides 520 mg/dL (high), cholesterol 40 mg/dL, and mostly lymphocytes. Gram stain shows no organisms. Injury to which structure most likely explains this fluid?
choices: Azygos vein
Esophageal anastomosis
Right main bronchus
Thoracic duct
Superior vena cava
questions.explanation: Milky fluid with **very high triglycerides** and many **lymphocytes** is **chyle**, so this is a **chylothorax**. The **thoracic duct** runs up the posterior mediastinum right beside the esophagus, so esophageal surgery can tear it; flow of chyle rises when the patient eats fat, because the duct carries **chylomicrons** from the gut. A leak from the esophageal anastomosis also drains into the chest, but it brings saliva and food with bacteria and usually causes fever, not sterile milky fluid.
questions.explanation_pt: Líquido leitoso com **triglicerídeos muito altos** e muitos **linfócitos** é **quilo**, então se trata de **quilotórax**. O **ducto torácico** sobe pelo mediastino posterior junto ao esôfago, por isso a cirurgia esofágica pode lesá-lo; o fluxo de quilo aumenta quando o paciente ingere gordura, pois o ducto transporta **quilomícrons** do intestino. A fístula da anastomose esofágica também drena para o tórax, mas traz saliva e alimento com bactérias e costuma causar febre, e não líquido leitoso estéril.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old man suddenly develops sharp left-sided chest pain and mild shortness of breath while watching television. He is 1.91 m tall and weighs 64 kg, and he smokes cigarettes. He has no history of lung disease or trauma. Blood pressure is 122/76 mm Hg, pulse is 96/min, and oxygen saturation is 95% on room air. Over the upper left chest, breath sounds are decreased and percussion is hyperresonant. The trachea is in the midline. Which lesion most likely caused his condition?
choices: Rupture of small air-filled blebs under the pleura at the lung apex
Destruction of whole acini from a deficiency of a protease inhibitor
Permanent widening of bronchi after many years of infection
A cavity from necrotizing pneumonia that opened into the pleura
A tear in the visceral pleura caused by a broken rib
questions.explanation: A tall, thin young man who smokes and has a sudden pneumothorax at rest with no known lung disease has a **primary spontaneous pneumothorax**. It comes from rupture of **subpleural blebs at the apex**, where the lung is stretched the most. Panacinar emphysema from alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency can also cause pneumothorax, but that would be a **secondary** pneumothorax in a patient with known lung disease, and the main damage is in the lower lobes.
questions.explanation_pt: Um homem jovem, alto e magro, tabagista, com pneumotórax súbito em repouso e sem doença pulmonar conhecida tem **pneumotórax espontâneo primário**. Ele resulta da ruptura de **bolhas subpleurais (*blebs*) no ápice**, onde o pulmão sofre maior distensão. O enfisema panacinar por deficiência de alfa-1 antitripsina também pode causar pneumotórax, mas seria um pneumotórax **secundário** em paciente com doença pulmonar conhecida, e a lesão principal fica nos lobos inferiores.

questions.stem: A 67-year-old woman had open gallbladder surgery 2 days ago. Because of abdominal pain, she breathes shallowly and avoids coughing. Today her temperature is 37.9°C and oxygen saturation is 91% on room air. Over the left lower chest, percussion is dull, tactile fremitus is decreased, and breath sounds are absent. The trachea is shifted to the left. Chest x-ray shows an opaque left lower lobe and a raised left hemidiaphragm. Which mechanism best explains this lung finding?
choices: Air that has entered the pleural space
Fluid in the pleural space pressing on the lung
Gas absorbed from alveoli behind a mucus plug
Bacterial exudate that fills the alveoli
Scar tissue that pulls the lung inward
questions.explanation: Shallow breathing and a weak cough after surgery let **mucus plug a bronchus**. The gas trapped beyond the plug is absorbed into the blood, so the lobe collapses (**resorption atelectasis**) and its lost volume pulls the trachea and diaphragm **toward** the affected side. A pleural effusion also gives a dull chest with decreased fremitus, but it adds volume to the chest and pushes the trachea **away** from the affected side.
questions.explanation_pt: A respiração superficial e a tosse fraca após a cirurgia permitem que uma **rolha de muco obstrua um brônquio**. O gás retido além da rolha é absorvido pelo sangue, o lobo colapsa (**atelectasia de reabsorção**) e a perda de volume puxa a traqueia e o diafragma **para o lado afetado**. O derrame pleural também causa macicez com frêmito diminuído, mas acrescenta volume ao tórax e desvia a traqueia **para o lado oposto**.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old man had a stab wound to the left chest 3 weeks ago. A chest tube drained a hemothorax and was removed after 5 days. He now has 4 days of fever, chills and left-sided chest pain. CT shows a walled-off left pleural fluid collection with a thick, enhancing pleural lining. Aspiration yields thick, yellow fluid with these results: pH 6.95, glucose 28 mg/dL (serum 110 mg/dL), LDH 1,800 U/L, and 68,000 white cells/μL, mostly neutrophils. Gram stain shows gram-positive cocci in clusters. Which process best explains the low pleural fluid pH and glucose?
choices: High hydrostatic pressure in the pulmonary capillaries
Low plasma oncotic pressure from loss of albumin
Leak of lymph from an injured thoracic duct
Glucose use and acid production by neutrophils and bacteria
Blockage of pleural lymphatic drainage by metastatic tumor cells
questions.explanation: Pus in the pleural space is an **empyema**. The huge number of **neutrophils and bacteria** burn glucose, largely by **anaerobic glycolysis**, and release **lactate and CO2**, so pleural **glucose and pH fall** while LDH rises. High hydrostatic or low oncotic pressure makes a **transudate**, which has a normal pH and a glucose close to the serum value.
questions.explanation_pt: Pus no espaço pleural é **empiema**. O enorme número de **neutrófilos e bactérias** consome glicose, em grande parte por **glicólise anaeróbia**, e libera **lactato e CO2**, então a **glicose e o pH pleurais caem** enquanto o LDH sobe. Pressão hidrostática alta ou pressão oncótica baixa produz **transudato**, que tem pH normal e glicose próxima à do soro.
